title: Rebase vendored waffle on stock bytecodealliance/waffle with a tail-call patch
description: Why: portal-pc-waffle 0.5.5 lacks stock's backend correctness fixes (two found: multi-value order, treeify soundness) and diverges too far to merge (29 conflicting files). Nassau, the only real frontend, needs only tail calls beyond stock. Plan: vendor stock c466056 (0.3.2), port ReturnCall/ReturnCallIndirect terminators, then whatever else clif2wasm needs to keep compiling (atomics operators, shared memory flag, 64-bit memarg offset) as local patches; keep the patch series documented in vendor/waffle/VENDORED.md. Acceptance: all clif2wasm tests pass on the stock-based vendor, tail-call fixtures included.
close_reason: vendored waffle rebased onto stock c466056 with tail calls, atomics, shared memory; all tests pass

title: waffle backend reverses multi-value call results
description: Why: any call returning 2+ values binds them in reverse order, and mixed-type returns (i32, i8) produce invalid wasm ('type mismatch: expected i64, found i32'). Repro: callee 'pair(i32)->i32,i32' returns (v0+v0, v0); caller gets (v0, v0+v0) although the exported callee returns the right order. Cause (verified): portal-pc-waffle 0.5.5 src/backend/mod.rs lower_inst emits LocalSet over ctx.locals.values[value] in output order, but the first local.set pops the top of the stack (the last output). Iterating .iter().rev() fixes it; verified with a local patch, all tests incl. the ignored multi_value_call_results_keep_their_order pass. Acceptance: fix upstream or carry a [patch.crates-io] fork, then un-ignore tests/modes.rs multi_value_call_results_keep_their_order and add i128-return and mixed-type cases.
close_reason: fixed in vendored waffle (upstream 0f64d1b cherry-picked); test un-ignored

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: Not present in stock bytecodealliance/waffle 0.3.2: its backend/mod.rs already iterates ctx.locals.values[value].iter().rev() before LocalSet. Regression is in portal-pc-waffle 0.5.5. Pure wasm round-trip repro (no clif2wasm): (func $pair (param i32) (result i32 i32) local.get 0 local.get 0 i32.add local.get 0) + main calling it and dropping the 2nd result: original 600, stock waffle 600, portal-pc-waffle 300. Repro crate: scratchpad mv/ (Cargo project with both deps).

title: Lower CLIF atomics through portal-pc-waffle
description: Lower representable CLIF atomic operations with portal-pc-waffle shared-memory Wasm operators. Keep atomic lowering outside the differential fixture suite because the chosen reference interpreter and Wasmi execution runtime cannot run the needed linear shared-memory atomics.
acceptance_criteria: Default translation rejects atomic CLIF unless shared memory is explicitly enabled; representable operations lower to Wasm atomics and unsupported operations fail clearly; atomic fixtures are intentionally absent with the limitation documented.
notes: Per user direction, removed the atomic smoke fixtures and runner special case. Atomics remain implemented but untested in the committed fixture suite.
close_reason: Atomic lowering is implemented; user-approved scope defers fixture coverage and documents why.

title: Prevent atomics from silently becoming ordinary memory operations
description:
## Context
Atomic load/store, read-modify-write, and compare-and-swap currently lower to ordinary wasm loads and stores. This is only correct under an explicit single-threaded execution contract. Until shared-memory atomics are implemented, reject atomic CLIF operations unless a documented single-thread mode is explicitly selected.

## Steps to Reproduce
Translate a CLIF function containing an atomic load, atomic store, atomic RMW, or atomic CAS and inspect or execute the emitted wasm. The current lowering emits non-atomic memory operations without requiring a single-thread setting.

## Acceptance Criteria
Default translation rejects every atomic opcode with a clear diagnostic. If a single-thread mode is supported, tests demonstrate it is opt-in and document that threaded wasm is unsupported. No atomic operation silently emits non-atomic wasm under the default configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Default translation rejects every atomic opcode with a clear diagnostic. If a single-thread mode is supported, tests demonstrate it is opt-in and document that threaded wasm is unsupported. No atomic operation silently emits non-atomic wasm under the default configuration.
close_reason: Reject atomic load/store/RMW/CAS and fence rather than lowering to non-atomic operations. Add error fixtures checked by the shared runner; cargo test passes.

title: Preserve i8 and i16 semantics across wasm lowering
description:
## Context
The translator maps CLIF i8/i16 values to wasm i32. Current lowering masks only narrow add/sub/mul results, while other operations can consume or produce values whose high bits affect later CLIF operations. Make narrow operand normalization and result truncation consistent across every supported opcode, including signed operations.

## Steps to Reproduce
Translate a function that takes an i8 or i16 parameter and uses it in a bitwise operation, shift, division, or comparison before returning or widening the result. Compare its execution with the Cranelift interpreter, especially for -1 and the type's signed minimum/maximum.

## Acceptance Criteria
Add differential fixtures covering narrow function arguments, bitwise operations, shifts, arithmetic, signed and unsigned comparisons, and narrowing conversions. Results and downstream uses must match the Cranelift interpreter for boundary values such as -1, minimum, and maximum.
acceptance_criteria: Add differential fixtures covering narrow function arguments, bitwise operations, shifts, arithmetic, signed and unsigned comparisons, and narrowing conversions. Results and downstream uses must match the Cranelift interpreter for boundary values such as -1, minimum, and maximum.
close_reason: Normalize i8/i16 arguments and operation operands/results; add differential fixtures for narrow arithmetic, bitwise, shifts, comparisons, extensions, counts, division, and truncation. cargo test passes.

title: Lower vector narrow, widen, demote and promote opcodes
description: Why: snarrow, unarrow, uunarrow, swiden_low/high, uwiden_low/high, fvdemote and fvpromote_low report unimplemented, yet wasm has direct operators (i8x16.narrow_i16x8, i16x8.extend_low_i8x16, f32x4.demote_f64x2_zero, f64x2.promote_low_f32x4). Scope: those nine opcodes across the lane types wasm covers, with a scalar legalization elsewhere or an explicit boundary. Acceptance: differential fixtures per opcode and docs/simd.md updated.
close_reason: Closed

title: Waffle gap: no wasm exception-handling operators
description: Why: waffle 0.5.5 has control tags in Module and a commented-out Handler per-tag design but no throw/rethrow/try_table operators or terminators (verified in src/ir/func.rs, src/ops.rs). This blocks real try_call handlers (aaw.10). Options: contribute or fork portal-pc-waffle to add EH, or lower try_call to a status-return ABI. Acceptance: decision recorded and linked from aaw.10.

title: Lower sextend/uextend i8 to i16
description: Why: probe of 'v1 = sextend.i16 v0' (i8 arg) fails with 'extend to i16 unimplemented' (E2000). Narrow ints live in i32 with a canonical zero-extended form, so this needs a sign-extend-narrow plus mask. Not a waffle limit. Acceptance: sextend and uextend among i8/i16/i32/i64 all lower, with differential tests including negative inputs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Code headers and agent instruction files
description: Replace lib.rs header (stale prototype question, cites missing docs/plans file) with real purpose + pointer to docs/architecture.md. Add //! single-responsibility header to modules lacking one. Fill CLAUDE.md placeholders (Build & Test, Architecture Overview, Conventions) and mirror in AGENTS.md.
acceptance_criteria: No module without a header; CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md carry no placeholders.

title: docs/testing.md
description: How to run tests; layers (differential fixtures vs interpreter and wasmi, '; wasm-run:' fixtures, '; fuzz: skip', tests/modes.rs, tests/object_link.rs); known flaky seed 0x5e355022; how to add a fixture.
acceptance_criteria: One page. Commands copy-paste runnable.

title: README.md
description: Replace 4-line README: what the tool is, minimal usage snippet, the three output modes, links to docs/.
acceptance_criteria: Under 60 lines.

title: docs/architecture.md
description: Pipeline CLIF -> waffle (bridge/ops) -> relocatable bodies with relocs -> link (whole module, session) or object (wasm-ld .o). Table of which file owns what. Why all modes share the relocatable core.
acceptance_criteria: One page. Every src/ module appears in the ownership table.

title: docs/relocatable-form.md
description: Invariants of relocatable.rs/link.rs: symbol index order (functions, libcalls, data, __stack_pointer, table), marker globals and 5-byte padded LEB splicing, reloc types incl. private R_CLIF2WASM_STACK_LIMIT 0xF0 (never written to objects), table policy (slot 0 null, ordinal k at k+1).
acceptance_criteria: One page. Each invariant names the code that enforces it.

title: docs/memory-and-modes.md
description: DATA_BASE 0x1000, 64 KiB shadow stack, prologue frame carve and limit check, session stack limit 4096. Table comparing whole-module vs object vs session: owner of memory/table/stack pointer, data address assignment, how earlier functions are imported.
acceptance_criteria: One page. Includes the mode comparison table.

title: Maintainer documentation
description: Focused docs so the translator can be maintained without reading all of src/. Each doc is one page or less, states invariants and ownership, and does not narrate code. Out of scope: per-function API docs, changelog, opcode-gap lists (tracked in aaw).

title: Fuzzer: generate arbitrary programs, not just fixture-derived ones
description: tests/support/fuzz.rs mostly fuzzes single opcodes and mutates inputs of existing fixtures. Add a generator for arbitrary well-formed CLIF functions (multi-block control flow incl. loops and br_table, block params, calls, stack slots, mixed int widths/i128/vectors) driven off Cranelift opcode metadata, run through cranelift-interpreter and wasmi as the differential oracle. Cover object mode, session mode and shared memory too, and use cranelift-fuzzgen ideas where possible.
acceptance_criteria: generated multi-block programs run differentially; coverage across all translation modes; failures minimize to a .clif fixture
notes: Known flake: CLIF2WASM_FUZZ_SEED=0x5e355022 cargo test --test differential supported_simple_opcodes panics in cranelift-interpreter step.rs:659 (Unsupported integer length 128). Reproduces on clean HEAD, so not caused by other changes. Generator hands i128 to ops the interpreter lacks; filter or route to wasm-run. Also: randomize_constants rewrites every iconst, so fixtures needing exact constants (loops) need '; fuzz: skip'.

title: Evaluate waffle WasmFuncBackend::compile for object.rs instead of harvesting bodies
description: object.rs builds one waffle module, calls to_wasm_bytes, harvests each body from the code section with wasmparser and splices marker global.gets into padded i32.const + relocs. Its header claims waffle's per-function backend is private, but waffle::backend is pub and WasmFuncBackend::compile(&FunctionBody) returns a wasm_encoder::Function. Determine whether per-function compile removes the harvest step, and what the real blocker is for reloc offsets (padded LEB128). Output: findings plus either a simplification or a documented reason.
acceptance_criteria: Written finding in the issue; object.rs simplified or comment corrected
notes: FINDINGS. (1) harvest_code_bodies re-parsed bytes that waffle's module compile had just produced via WasmFuncBackend::compile(body).into_raw_body(); the 'per-function backend is private' header was stale (waffle::backend is pub in 0.5.5). object.rs now calls it per body: no whole-module encode, no marker-global/data/elem sections generated and thrown away, no parse-back. (2) The splicer cannot go away by using the per-function API: wasm-ld needs 5-byte padded LEBs at reloc sites and waffle/wasm-encoder only write minimal LEBs, with no hook. Removing it needs our own emitter (or a padded-LEB option upstreamed into the waffle fork) - input for the waffle-vs-direct decision under clif2wasm-srz. (3) BUG found: after clif2wasm-5t2, object mode emitted return_call/return_call_indirect and splice_body copied them verbatim (no FUNCTION_INDEX/TYPE_INDEX/TABLE_NUMBER relocs); wasm-ld crashed on the indirect form and the direct form only worked when the callee index was unchanged. Fixed in splice_body and tail-call target feature is declared only when used. (4) Object mode had validation-only tests; tests/object_link.rs now links with wasm-ld (padding object first to force renumbering) and runs on wasmi; skipped when wasm-ld is absent.
close_reason: per-function compile adopted in object.rs; splicer retained (needs padded LEBs); return_call reloc bug fixed; wasm-ld link tests added

title: Unify whole-module, object and session translation paths
description: module.rs, object.rs and the emit_incremental session mode are selected by Option checks (layout.is_some, object_markers.is_some, shared_memory) spread over module.rs/bridge.rs/ops.rs, with duplicated undefined-symbol policy and no tail calls in object mode. Make object mode (symbol markers + relocs) the single translation path and turn whole-module and session into small linkers that place data and assign table slots. Also lets define_function translate eagerly instead of buffering all ir::Functions until finish().
acceptance_criteria: one translate_function path; whole-module output produced by linking object output; all fixtures pass in all modes
notes: Done: all modes go relocatable::translate then link::link (or object writer). Not done: eager translation at define_function.
close_reason: Closed

title: Replace tail-call marker rewrite with waffle ReturnCall terminators
description: bridge.rs/module.rs emit a __tail_marker function and tail.rs reparses the whole module to turn 'call marker' into return_call. waffle 0.5.5 already has Terminator::ReturnCall/ReturnCallIndirect and lowers them (backend/stackify.rs). Switch to those, delete tail.rs, the marker funcs and ModCtx.tail_calls. Check git log for why the marker approach was chosen first. Verify with existing tail-call fixtures and fuzz tests.
acceptance_criteria: tail.rs removed; no __tail_marker functions in output; tail-call fixtures and fuzz tests pass
close_reason: tail.rs and marker functions removed; waffle ReturnCall terminators used; new fixtures tail_call_loop/tail_call_indirect_loop run 1M-deep loops with a stack slot

title: Add supported-CLIF randomized differential test generator
description: Create a test-only generator that builds valid Cranelift functions from the subset clif2wasm supports, then use the existing Cranelift interpreter and Wasm runtime to check translation behavior across deterministic randomized cases.
notes:
Added metadata-driven generation for Cranelift Unary, Binary, Ternary, IntCompare, and FloatCompare formats; generated operand types come from Cranelift opcode constraints. The fixture corpus fuzz pass now randomizes constant pool/immediate constants and ABI inputs for every non-error fixture, using interpreter comparisons where available and Wasm execution for wasm-run-only fixtures. Remaining audit: specialized instruction formats (memory, atomics, calls, shuffle/immediates, and multi-result operations) need explicit generators or a verified fixture-backed path.
Added dedicated generated differential coverage for StackAddr (varying stack size, offset, and value) and object-mode SymbolValue (varying data-symbol offset, validated as wasm object). The test-only harness remains in tests/support/fuzz.rs; generic opcode formats are metadata-driven, with special formats handled by dedicated generators or existing fixture fuzzing. SymbolValue object-mode test and StackAddr test pass.
Expanded metadata-driven simple opcode generation from the first supported control type to every candidate type accepted by Cranelift constraints and supported by the translator. This exposed invalid Wasm for scalar-to-vector fcvt_to_{sint,uint}_sat and fcvt_from_{sint,uint}; translator now rejects those unsupported combinations explicitly. The expanded generator and focused tests pass.
Expanded memory opcode generation to try every supported control type instead of stopping at the first successful type. Generated memory matrix validates and executes successfully.
Fixture randomizer now includes valid trap fixtures under tests/fixtures/error and excludes only fixtures explicitly annotated with translation errors. This fuzzes randomized i128 division trap and overflow cases.
Added generated in-memory direct and indirect return_call cases. The indirect case exposed invalid Wasm because the i64 callee pointer was not wrapped to the marker's i32 table-index parameter; bridge lowering now wraps it consistently with call_indirect.
Added in-memory direct and indirect return_call generators and validation. The indirect generator caught and fixed a missing i64-to-i32 table-index conversion in bridge lowering. Both tail-call paths now validate.
Added exhaustive InstructionFormat routing audit: every Cranelift opcode format is assigned to metadata generation, fixture-driven generation, a specialized generator, or an explicit unsupported classification. ExtractVector remains explicitly skipped because the current translator has no lowering for it and its dynamic-vector constraints cannot be represented in this fixed candidate generator.
close_reason: Added opcode-format coverage routing and generators for all currently supported formats, with metadata-driven sweeps and fixture-backed special cases; full test suite passes.

title: Complete remaining i128 high multiply, conversions, and carry operations
description: Implement the remaining documented i128 gaps: smulhi/umulhi, float conversions where semantics permit, and add/sub carry/borrow input overflow forms. Add fixtures for supported cases and explicit diagnostic fixtures for any forms that remain unsupported.
notes:
Implemented i128 signed/unsigned high multiply, all four carry/borrow input overflow forms, correctly rounded i128-to-f32/f64 conversions, and saturating f32/f64-to-i128 conversions. Trapping float-to-i128 conversion remains explicitly unsupported with an error fixture. Fixtures cover cross-limb multiplication, ties-to-even, conversion bounds, carry normalization, and overflow. Full checks pass.
Follow-up validation confirmed carry/borrow overflow flags combine the base and follow-up overflow flags with OR, matching CLIF semantics; added regression coverage.
close_reason: Completed the remaining supported i128 gaps and documented/tested trapping conversion limitation.

title: Unify module translation behind Cranelift Module interface
description: Why: callers currently choose between slice-based translate_module APIs and the optional WasmModule Module-trait adapter. Most compiler integrations already have Cranelift declarations, so maintaining two assembly interfaces creates friction and duplicated paths. Make WasmModule the single public module assembly interface, available without a feature flag, and adapt tests/docs. Acceptance: no module-seam feature gate; the crate builds with Module integration enabled by default; public assembly flows through WasmModule; fixture behavior remains covered.
acceptance_criteria: Only one caller-facing module assembly interface remains, available by default, and existing fixture coverage passes.
notes: Unified Wasm module assembly behind the root-level WasmModule implementing cranelift_module::Module. Removed slice-based translate_module APIs and their helper wrappers, removed the module-seam feature gate, made cranelift-module and Pulley support unconditional, and moved translation options/runtime overrides/import aliases onto WasmModule. Differential fixtures now declare and define CLIF functions through the same interface. Verified cargo fmt --check, cargo test, cargo check --all-features, and git diff --check.
close_reason: WasmModule is now the sole public wasm assembly interface and is enabled by default

title: Introduce typed diagnostics with thiserror and miette
description: Why: Translation currently reports most failures through anyhow::bail!, which makes errors difficult to classify and present with source context.\n\nAcceptance: Define typed translation errors with thiserror, attach relevant CLIF instruction/function context with miette diagnostics, preserve useful error chains for callers, and migrate current bail-style failure paths without losing established diagnostic text or fixture behavior.
notes: Completed typed error migration. Public Error has Internal, Unsupported, and Error categories; thiserror preserves causes and miette attaches synthesized CLIF function/instruction source spans. Stable ErrorCode values are explicit numeric IDs (e.g. UnsupportedOpcode = 2000 => CLIF2WASM-E2000), verified by the unsupported vector fixture. Removed direct anyhow dependency and all anyhow references from Cargo.toml/src; remaining lockfile entries are transitive through Cranelift/Waffle. Verified with cargo fmt --check, cargo test, cargo check --all-features, and cargo check --features module-seam.
close_reason: Migrated translation errors to thiserror/miette with stable diagnostic codes and no direct anyhow use

title: Handle CLIF immediate-form scalar opcodes
description:
Why: An alternate generated Cranelift 0.136 opcode inventory includes immediate-form arithmetic, comparison, shift, rotate, division/remainder, and bitwise opcodes not named in the current translator.

Scope: iadd_imm, imul_imm, irsub_imm, icmp_imm, signed/unsigned div/rem immediate forms, immediate shifts/rotates, band/bor/bxor immediate and complement forms.

Acceptance: Confirm which forms are exposed by the configured Cranelift Opcode::all(); lower all exposed supported forms with correct signedness and overflow behavior, and cover them in opcode inventory/tests.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: Probe: iadd_imm is an unknown opcode in the configured cranelift-reader (parse failure), so immediate forms may not be exposed in 0.136. Confirm against Opcode::all() before lowering.

title: Support explicit stack load/store opcodes
description:
Why: An alternate generated Cranelift 0.136 opcode inventory includes stack_load, stack_store, dynamic_stack_load, and dynamic_stack_store forms not covered by the current stack_addr path.

Acceptance: Confirm these forms are exposed by the configured Cranelift Opcode::all(); lower supported accesses with correct frame/dynamic-stack semantics or document why they are outside the backend contract; tests cover supported forms.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower scalar fused multiply-add
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines scalar fma, which is not covered by current float lowering.

Acceptance: f32/f64 fma preserve single-rounding behavior; tests distinguish fused from separate multiply/add.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: Probe: scalar f32 fma fails 'unimplemented opcode fma'. Wasm has no scalar fma; needs a software routine or libcall. Vector fma is a separate bead.

title: Handle sequence points
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines sequence_point, whose treatment by this Wasm backend needs to be explicit.

Acceptance: The opcode has a documented handling policy and a coverage test or rationale for safe erasure.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower integer overflow and carry operations
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines overflow and carry operations that are not covered by existing lowering tasks.

Scope: sadd_overflow_cin, uadd_overflow_cin, signed/unsigned add, subtract, and multiply overflow operations, trapping overflow variants, and overflow-with-borrow forms.

Acceptance: Each supported opcode/type combination returns the correct value and overflow result or traps as specified; tests cover signed and unsigned boundaries.

title: Lower cls and bmask integer operations
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines cls and bmask, which have no lowering in the current translator.

Acceptance: Supported widths match Cranelift semantics, with tests for zero, sign patterns, and boundary values; unsupported widths have explicit diagnostics.
close_reason: Closed

title: Lower conditional traps
description:
Why: Cranelift 0.136 defines trapz and trapnz, but current control-flow lowering handles unconditional trap only.

Acceptance: Both opcodes translate correctly for supported integer widths; tests cover true/false conditions and trap codes.
close_reason: trapz/trapnz done with aaw.12 (i32 tested; other widths go through coerce_cond); trap code reporting stays in aaw.26

title: Lower remaining select and target-specific operations
description:
Why: Handle select_spectre_guard, bitselect, blendv, and x86 pshufb/pmulhrsw where supported by the selected legalization strategy.

Acceptance: Applicable operations preserve semantics; machine-specific operations are legalized independent of host ISA or explicitly rejected with tests.
close_reason: select_spectre_guard, x86_pmaddubsw and x86_cvtt2dq lowered; bitselect, blendv, pshufb, pmulhrsw already covered; fixtures added

title: Add opcode and type coverage audit for Cranelift upgrades
description: Why: Source inspection shows Cranelift exposes Opcode::all() for the version pinned by this crate. Generated build artifacts also differed in opcode count, so the inventory must reflect the actual dependency configuration rather than a hand-copied list.\n\nAcceptance: Add a coverage registry with an explicit status for every Opcode::all() member in the configured build (lowered, intentionally erased, or unsupported with rationale). Ensure a Cranelift upgrade or configuration change that adds an opcode forces inventory review. Track partial type/feature support and document the refresh workflow.
close_reason: tests/opcode_coverage.txt plus tests/opcode_inventory.rs; docs/opcode-coverage.md; new bead aaw.33 for narrow/widen/demote/promote

title: Complete tail-call lowering
description:
Why: Tail-call lowering has gaps across supported call forms, signatures, and modes.

Scope: return_call and return_call_indirect, imports, libcalls, object mode, Wasm feature constraints, and shadow-stack cleanup.

Acceptance: Supported tail calls lower correctly; unsupported feature/ABI cases report specific errors; tests cover direct and indirect calls.
notes: Direct and indirect return_call now use waffle Terminator::ReturnCall/ReturnCallIndirect (clif2wasm-5t2); TestCase callees resolve. Object mode no longer hard-fails on a missing tail map, but is untested - verify.
close_reason: direct, indirect, import, multi-value, object-mode tail calls tested; libcall tail call reports a specific error

title: Lower traps, debug traps, and machine state intrinsics
description:
Why: Machine-specific and trap operations require explicit Wasm/runtime semantics.

Scope: debugtrap, trap, trapz, trapnz, pinned-register operations, frame/stack/return-address access, exception-handler-address operations, and related intrinsics where meaningful for Wasm. Conditional trap work is also tracked in clif2wasm-aaw.15.

Acceptance: Each opcode has a correct Wasm/runtime lowering or an explicit documented unsupported boundary with tests.
close_reason: debugtrap no-op, trapz/trapnz, get_stack_pointer lowered; pinned reg, frame pointer, return address, handler address rejected with specific errors; docs/machine-state.md

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: Probe: debugtrap, get_stack_pointer, get_return_address, get_pinned_reg, get_frame_pointer, trapz, trapnz all fail 'unimplemented opcode'. get_stack_pointer (shadow-stack global) and pinned reg (a wasm global) look implementable; frame/return address have no wasm equivalent. Plain 'trap user5' already works but drops the code (see trap-code bead).

title: Support try_call and exception control flow
description:
Why: The bridge does not handle try_call/try_call_indirect exception edges and exception tables.

Acceptance: Supported exceptional control flow translates with correct block arguments and results and has tests; unsupported models are explicitly diagnosed and documented.
close_reason: try_call/try_call_indirect without handlers lowered to call+branch; handler tables diagnosed E2000 and documented in docs/exceptions.md; handler support tracked in aaw.31; multi-value results blocked on clif2wasm-opi

comments.author: Takashiidobe
comments.text: Probe (waffle 0.5.5): try_call with any exception table errors 'unimplemented opcode try_call'. With an empty handler list ([]) it needs no EH: lower as plain call plus branch to the normal-return block. Handlers need EH operators waffle lacks; see the waffle-gap bead.

title: Lower dynamic stack addresses and stack switching
description:
Why: dynamic_stack_addr and stack_switch are not currently lowered.

Acceptance: Stack operations have a documented ABI/runtime design and correct tests, or precise unsupported diagnostics and rationale.
close_reason: Documented unsupported stack-operation runtime requirements and added precise diagnostics with source-span fixtures

title: Support TLS and remaining global value forms
description:
Why: Global lowering currently handles limited symbol forms and excludes TLS/dynamic forms.

Scope: tls_value and applicable GlobalValueData forms beyond direct symbols, including dynamic or VMContext forms.

Acceptance: Every intended form resolves correctly or has an explicit documented boundary; tests cover symbol offsets, TLS policy, and object mode.
close_reason: boundary: only symbol globals lower; tls and non-symbol forms rejected with E2000, tls data declarations rejected; tests + docs/global-values.md

title: Complete floating-point and narrow conversion coverage
description:
Why: Several float conversion forms and f16/f128 types are not currently supported.

Scope: Missing constants and conversions where Waffle/Wasm can represent or legalize them, plus narrow and i128 float-to-int cases and i128-to-float conversions where possible.

Acceptance: Lowerings preserve NaN, overflow, saturation, and trap behavior, or document the unsupported boundary; tests cover edge cases.
close_reason: Added differential coverage for narrow float conversions and documented unsupported float conversion boundaries

title: Support remaining scalar memory operations and flags
description:
Why: Current memory lowering covers common scalar accesses but not all CLIF access forms or flag combinations.

Scope: Remaining widening/truncating and vector loads/stores where supported, plus memory flags, alignment, offsets, and endianness.

Acceptance: Supported combinations lower correctly; unsupported flags and offsets fail explicitly; tests cover widths and boundaries.
close_reason: Validated memory flags, rejected unsupported big-endian accesses, guarded split offsets, and added memory fixtures

title: Lower SIMD arithmetic, comparisons, and reductions
description:
Why: Cranelift's vector opcode families are absent from the current scalar lowering.

Scope: vector arithmetic and bitwise ops, comparisons, select/blendv/bitselect, reductions (vany_true, vall_true, vhigh_bits), pairwise add, multiply/add variants, and vector float conversion operations where supported.

Acceptance: Supported SIMD families preserve lane semantics; tests cover each selected opcode family and lane type. Unsupported cases are explicit.
notes: Implemented chunkwise SIMD arithmetic/bitwise lowering, vector comparisons (including unsigned i64 via sign-bit bias), select/blendv/bitselect, lane-wise shifts/rotates and fcopysign legalization, integer absolute value, pairwise add, signed/unsigned high multiply, any/all/high-bit reductions, and Wasm-supported vector float conversions/unary operations. Added fixture coverage across i8/i16/i32/i64/f32/f64 families, including saturation, comparison, reductions, pairwise add, mulhi, shifts, blend/select, bitselect, float arithmetic, and conversions. Updated docs/simd.md with supported forms and explicit unsupported boundaries. Reader rejects vector division syntax before translation; Wasm SIMD has no fused multiply-add instruction, so these remain unsupported.
close_reason: Implemented SIMD arithmetic, comparisons, selections, reductions, and supported conversions with fixture coverage

title: Complete scalar integer min/max, saturation, and multiply operations
description:
Why: Scalar integer min/max, saturation, rounded average, and high multiply opcodes are missing from current lowering.

Scope: smin, umin, smax, umax, uadd_sat, sadd_sat, usub_sat, ssub_sat, avg_round, umulhi, smulhi, and applicable rounded/saturating multiply instructions.

Acceptance: Supported opcode/type combinations lower correctly and have focused tests; unsupported combinations fail with specific diagnostics.
notes: Implemented scalar smin/umin/smax/umax and smulhi/umulhi for valid scalar integer widths. Added vector avg_round, sqmul_round_sat, and x86_pmulhrsw lowerings plus fixture coverage. Confirmed Cranelift rejects scalar saturation and scalar avg_round as invalid CLIF types; the valid vector forms are tested. All fixtures pass.
close_reason: Implemented all valid scalar and related vector integer special-op combinations with fixture coverage.

title: Complete i128 arithmetic and conversion coverage
description:
Why: Current i128 support uses i64 pairs and covers only selected operations.

Scope: Remaining meaningful integer operations including div/rem, high multiply, abs, min/max, overflow/saturation, and float conversions where semantics permit.

Acceptance: Every intended i128 opcode is lowered or explicitly documented unsupported; tests cover carries, signedness, overflow, division corners, and conversions.
notes: Added i128 unsigned/signed div/rem with divide-by-zero and signed overflow traps, signed/unsigned min/max, and add/sub overflow flags. Added docs/i128.md listing the remaining unsupported high-multiply and float-conversion cases, plus fixture coverage for carries, borrow, signedness, overflows, division corners, and unsupported diagnostics. All checks pass.
close_reason: Completed supported i128 arithmetic and documented/tested remaining unsupported operations.

title: Choose SIMD representation and legalization strategy
description:
Why: Choose a representation and legalization strategy for CLIF vectors, which have no direct scalar representation in the current bridge.

Acceptance: Document vector value representation, lane order, supported widths/types, legalizations, and unsupported boundaries.
design:
Representation: extend the CLIF value map with a vector bundle: an ordered low-to-high list of Waffle V128 values. Keep scalar values as one Waffle value and i128 as its existing pair. Each bundle element represents 128 consecutive bits, with lane 0 in the least-significant bits of the first chunk, matching Wasm SIMD lane numbering and little-endian memory layout.

Fixed widths: map 64-bit CLIF vectors to one V128 with the unused upper 64 bits canonicalized to zero; map 128-bit vectors directly to one V128; map 256- and 512-bit vectors to two or four V128 chunks. Legalize lane-wise operators per chunk and explicitly normalize padding bits for sub-128-bit vectors. Cross-chunk shuffle, reductions, and other operations need operation-specific lowering.

Initial direct lane shapes: i8, i16, i32, i64, f32, and f64, matching Wasm SIMD. Other CLIF lane types may use V128 as raw bits, but arithmetic/conversions without equivalent Wasm operators remain unsupported until a separate legalization is implemented. Dynamic/scalable CLIF vectors are rejected because Wasm v128 has a fixed width and cannot represent a runtime-scaled number of lanes without a different loop/runtime ABI.

Validation: keep CLIF error fixtures for unsupported cases; when a fixture translates, the harness instructs the contributor to promote it into tests/fixtures and add interpreter-versus-Wasm run expectations. Wasmi's SIMD feature is enabled for all test builds.
notes: Investigation confirmed Waffle 0.5.5 exposes Type::V128 and SIMD Operator variants, its backend emits wasm_encoder SIMD instructions, and its package includes tests/roundtrip/test-simd.wat. SIMD support exists in Wasm and Waffle; the challenge is representing CLIF vector widths and legalizing operations. The chosen bundle representation and fixed/scalable width boundaries are recorded in Design. Current map_type rejects CLIF vectors. The error fixture tests this current boundary; promotion to regular fixtures is signaled by the harness. Wasmi SIMD support is enabled in the shared dev dependency.
close_reason: Recorded SIMD representation and legalization design based on Cranelift and Waffle capabilities; added fixture coverage for the current unsupported boundary.

title: Lower SIMD constants, splat, lanes, and shuffles
description:
Why: Cranelift vectors have no direct scalar representation in the current bridge.

Scope: vconst, scalar_to_vector, extract_vector, splat, shuffle, swizzle, x86_pshufb, insertlane, extractlane, vector load forms, and lane widening/narrowing operations where the chosen representation permits them.

Acceptance: Documented supported vector combinations lower correctly; tests cover lane order and boundaries; unsupported cases are explicit.
notes: Implemented fixed-width vector bundles and SIMD lowering for vconst, scalar_to_vector, splat, insertlane, extractlane, shuffle, swizzle, x86_pshufb, vector bitcast, vector load/store, and widening vector-load forms. Added differential fixtures for constants, lane boundaries, shuffle/swizzle, calls, direct vector memory, and Wasm-only pshufb. Dynamic vectors remain explicitly rejected; cross-chunk shuffle and unsupported lane legalization remain outside this implementation. Widening-load CLIF fixture parsing could not be validated: cranelift-reader rejects uload8x8.i16x8 before translation.
close_reason: Implemented documented fixed-width SIMD representation and lowering with fixture coverage for the supported combinations and boundaries.

title: Complete CLIF 0.136 to Waffle instruction coverage
description:
Why: clif2wasm currently lowers a scalar subset of Cranelift 0.136 CLIF and errors on other valid instructions or type combinations. This epic tracks the remaining instruction and representation work required for broad CLIF-to-Waffle translation. Scope includes scalar, i128, SIMD, memory, control flow, and machine-specific CLIF operations; Wasm-inexpressible semantics need explicit legalization or a documented boundary.

Acceptance: Every Cranelift 0.136 opcode is either lowered correctly for supported types and semantics, or intentionally rejected with a documented reason and coverage test. Tests cover each newly supported family.

title: Spike portal-pc-waffle dependency swap for atomics
description: Determine whether portal-pc-waffle can replace waffle with manageable API changes and support shared-memory atomic emission. Build the project and validate representative atomic instructions plus shared memory configuration.
acceptance_criteria: Project compiles against portal-pc-waffle; representative atomic operators can be represented and encoded; shared memory with maximum validates; summarize migration cost and recommend whether to keep or revert the swap.
notes: The spike smoke test was temporary and was removed during the completed dependency transition, per user direction. The portal-pc-waffle dependency and API adapters remain in place.
close_reason: The portal-pc-waffle 0.5.5 swap compiles after adapting changed signature, memory, table, and reference type APIs. Added a smoke test proving shared memory with a maximum plus atomic RMW/CAS are emitted and validate. Full cargo test and diff check pass.

title: Support multi-function differential fixtures and call coverage
description: The fixture runner currently requires exactly one CLIF function, which prevents end-to-end tests of direct calls, indirect calls, and shared function-index resolution. Extend fixture loading and interpreter setup to register all parsed functions and translate them as one module.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with multiple functions can invoke a selected exported entry point. Add direct-call and call_indirect cases whose results match both the fixture expectation and the Cranelift interpreter. Include clear diagnostics for unresolved fixture function references.
close_reason: Fixture runner now supports multiple CLIF functions and selectable entries; direct and indirect calls match interpreter/wasm results, and unresolved fixture callees have a diagnostic regression fixture.

title: Add differential coverage for CLIF memory operations and stack slots
description: Current fixtures exercise scalar returns but do not cover the translator's load/store and shadow-stack paths. Add CLIF fixtures using stack_addr and stack slots so memory behavior can be checked by both the Cranelift interpreter and wasm runtime.
acceptance_criteria: Cover load/store offsets, narrow signed and unsigned loads, truncating stores, and stack-slot frame setup. Each fixture compares the interpreter and wasm results and checks explicit expected values; emitted wasm validates before execution.
close_reason: Added differential fixtures for stack frame setup, offset load/store, signed and unsigned narrow loads, and truncating stores; Wasmi validates and executes each module against Cranelift interpreter results.

title: Compare expected traps in differential CLIF fixtures
description: The fixture runner currently treats a trap in either runtime as a harness failure, so it cannot test CLIF traps or wasm trap equivalence. Add a fixture directive for expected traps and compare interpreter and wasm outcomes.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures can declare a call expected to trap. The runner passes when both Cranelift interpretation and wasm execution trap, and reports a useful failure when only one traps or either returns. Cover explicit trap and integer division by zero.
close_reason: Added ; trap: fixture directives and differential outcome checks; explicit void/value traps and signed division by zero trap in both engines.

title: Handle unreachable CLIF blocks during function translation
description:
## Context
The bridge creates a waffle block for every laid-out CLIF block but only translates blocks in reachable CFG reverse postorder. Unreachable blocks can therefore be left without terminators, causing later validation or emission failures. Give unreachable blocks an explicit translation policy.

## Steps to Reproduce
Translate a function with an entry block that returns and a second laid-out block with a valid terminator that has no incoming edge. The block is allocated in waffle but omitted from reachable CFG translation.

## Acceptance Criteria
A valid function containing an unreachable laid-out block either translates to valid wasm with the unreachable block terminated, or fails during preflight with a clear unsupported-input error. Add a differential fixture and validate the emitted module.
acceptance_criteria: A valid function containing an unreachable laid-out block either translates to valid wasm with the unreachable block terminated, or fails during preflight with a clear unsupported-input error. Add a differential fixture and validate the emitted module.
close_reason: Unreachable laid-out blocks without translated terminators now receive an explicit unreachable terminator; differential fixture validates and executes the emitted wasm.

title: Guard against reducify code blowup on irreducible CFGs
description: Why: probe of an irreducible CLIF CFG translates fine (waffle reducify pass duplicates blocks), but waffle's docs warn of exponential code-size blowup for state machines and cliques. Acceptance: add irreducible fixtures with differential tests, measure growth on a larger state machine, and decide whether to cap block growth with a clear error, or add a relooper-style fallback upstream.

title: 64-bit pointer (memory64) translation mode
description: Why: CLIF built for 64-bit pointers fails the address tripwire (E1000 'address has CLIF type i64'). waffle has Memory.memory64 and 64-bit load/store address typing in op_traits.rs, so this may be feasible. Open questions: ModCtx/linker/relocation assumptions of i32 addresses, shadow stack pointer type, table indices, host engine support. Acceptance: design note on feasibility; if feasible, a mode flag with differential tests, else a documented boundary.

title: Vector fma (f32x4, f64x2 and wider) lowering
description: Why: probe of fma.f64x2 fails 'unimplemented opcode fma'. aaw.18 covers scalar fma only. Wasm has fused multiply-add only through relaxed-simd (f32x4.relaxed_madd), which is allowed to be unfused, and waffle 0.5.5 has no relaxed-simd operators (verified: none in src/ops.rs). Lanewise scalar fma per aaw.18 is the portable route. Acceptance: vector fma single-rounds per lane; decide whether to prefer relaxed-simd if waffle gains it.

title: Report CLIF user trap codes to the host
description: Why: probe of 'trap user5' translates, but wasm 'unreachable' carries no code, so TrapCode::User(n) and the Cranelift trap kinds (heap_oob, int_divz, ...) are indistinguishable at runtime. Options: call an imported env trap(code) before unreachable, or a distinct trap per code. Acceptance: chosen policy documented in docs, covers trap, trapz/trapnz (aaw.15), and checked-arithmetic traps, with tests that observe the code.

title: Lower big-endian loads and stores via byte swap
description: Why: big-endian load/store currently fail with E1000 ('big-endian load is unsupported'). Not a waffle limit: wasm memory is little-endian, but bswap32/bswap64 helpers already exist in ops/int.rs. Scope: load/store (scalar, narrow, i128, atomics decided separately). Acceptance: big-endian scalar accesses round-trip under differential tests; vector and atomic big-endian accesses are lowered or explicitly diagnosed.

title: Drop Pulley backend dependency used as pointer-width oracle
description: WasmModule::isa() returns a pulley32 TargetIsa solely so pointer_type()==I32. cranelift-codegen is built with the pulley feature, pulling a full backend into what should be a small browser-hostable build. Replace with a minimal custom TargetIsa or other approach, and measure wasm32 build size before/after. Also move CLIF2WASM_LENIENT / CLIF2WASM_IMPORTS env reads (not meaningful on wasm32-unknown-unknown) into TranslationOptions.
acceptance_criteria: pulley feature removed from Cargo.toml; Module::isa still gives I32 pointers; env vars replaced by options
notes: Pulley half blocked: cranelift-codegen 0.136 TargetIsa cannot be implemented outside the crate. IsaFlagsHashKey has a private field and no constructor, and compile_function returns CompiledCodeStencil, a type alias in private mod machinst that lib.rs does not re-export. Options: upstream a cranelift patch (constructible IsaFlagsHashKey, export CompiledCodeStencil), fork cranelift-codegen, or drop the cranelift_module::Module trait (breaks the nassau seam). Left as-is: pulley feature stays. Env half done: CLIF2WASM_LENIENT is now TranslationOptions::lenient; CLIF2WASM_IMPORTS removed (use allow_import).

title: Split ops.rs by domain
description: ops.rs is ~4000 lines in one lower_inst match with per-type cascades (e.g. icmp ten arms of if is64). Split into modules (int, float, mem, call, atomic, simd, i128) and make common cases table-driven (Opcode, wasm type) -> Operator. Pure refactor, no behavior change. Also add a test that fails when a Cranelift opcode is neither lowered nor listed as unsupported (known missing today: trapz, trapnz, uadd_overflow_trap, sextend/uextend i8->i16).
acceptance_criteria: ops split into submodules; tests unchanged and passing; opcode coverage test exists
notes: The opcode-coverage test overlaps clif2wasm-aaw.14; do it there, keep this issue to the pure split.
close_reason: ops.rs split into ops/{mod,int,vector,i128,cmp,select,mem,atomic,call}; opcode coverage test deferred to clif2wasm-aaw.14 per notes

title: Waffle gap: no relaxed-simd or stack-switching operators
description: Why: waffle 0.5.5 lacks relaxed-simd operators (relaxed madd/nmadd, relaxed trunc, laneselect, dot) and typed-continuation operators (cont.new, resume, suspend). stack_switch is therefore a hard boundary (docs/stack-operations.md) and vector fma cannot use relaxed madd. Acceptance: track upstream status; revisit stack_switch only if waffle and the target runtimes both support continuations.

title: Support f16 and f128 CLIF types
description: Why: probes show f16 and f128 signatures fail with E2001 'unsupported CLIF type'. Wasm has neither. f16 could be soft-lowered through f32 with exact conversions (double rounding hazards for arithmetic); f128 needs libcall-style soft float. Acceptance: decide per type between soft lowering and documented boundary; if lowered, tests cover conversions, const, load/store, arithmetic.
close_reason: f16 soft-lowered via i32 bits and f32/f64 conversions; f128 documented boundary (docs/f16.md)
